deep.reconstruction:
This is a printed textbook page, almost certainly Christian Leiste's school 'Arithmetik und Algebra' (bundle 'HB.Leiste'). None of the printed text on it is by Gauss. The handwriting visible at the right edge (∫x^.../(1+..., 'sin. lem...', '1 1, 1/2 0,6.., 1/3 0,4..') is the cut-off left margin of the facing page 93. Those are Gauss's notes on the lemniscatic sine and integrals of the form ∫x^{a-1}dx/(1+x^b)^c, transcribed with the next page.

(i) End of §179, example 3 from p.91. Three numbers satisfy x+y=a, x+z=b, y+z=c. The general solution is y=(a-b+c)/2, x=(a+b-c)/2, z=(b+c-a)/2. With a=12, b=16, c=14 this gives y=(12-16+14)/2=5, x=(12+16-14)/2=7 and z=(16+14-12)/2=9. Check: 7+5=12, 7+9=16, 5+9=14.

(ii) §180, solving a pure equation x^m=A. The solution is x=A^(1/m), or equivalently log x=(1/m) log A. Case analysis by the number of real ('mögliche') roots:
- A>0, m even: two real roots ±A^(1/m) and m-2 complex ('unmögliche') roots.
- A>0, m odd (m=2n+1): one real root and m-1=2n complex roots.
- A<0, m even: all roots complex.
- A<0, m=2n+1: one real root and 2n complex roots.
The page then states that the 2n-th root of A is ± the square root of the n-th root of A, i.e. A^(1/(2n))=(A^(1/n))^(1/2). It also states that the odd root of -A is minus the odd root of A, (-A)^(1/(2n+1))=-A^(1/(2n+1)). Example: 64^(1/6)=sqrt(64^(1/3))=sqrt(4)=2.

(iii) §181, corollary. With x=z+a, the equation (z+a)^m=A is still pure in x. [My completion:] z=A^(1/m)-a.

(iv) §182, the general ('unreine') quadratic ax^2+bx+c=0. Dividing by the leading coefficient a gives x^2+(b/a)x+c/a=0, written B) x^2+px+q=0 with p and q arbitrary real numbers. The solution follows on p.93.
errors: No substantive errors on this page; all counts of real and complex roots and the numerical example are correct.
Notational looseness: '√[2n]{+A} = ±x' mixes the root value with the unknown x, and '√[n]{+A^{1/2}}' is ambiguous as to which root applies first (harmless for A>0).
The printed solution on the preceding page contains a misprint, 'a-b = x+y-x+z = y+z', which should read y-z. The final formulas, and the example on this page, are nevertheless correct.

transcription_corrections: The machine transcription omits the cut-off handwritten fragments in the right edge of the image ('∫ x^…/(1+…', '∫ x^…/(1-…', '∫', 'sin. lem…' twice, and the column '1 1, / 1/2 0,6… / 1/3 0,4…'). These belong to the margin of the facing page 93 (lemniscatic sine notes), not to this printed page.
'\sqrt[n]{+A^{\frac{1}{2}}}' matches the print, which shows the n-th root sign over '+ A^{1/2}'. The intended meaning is the n-th root combined with a square root, consistent with '= √ · ⁿ√A'.
In '\sqrt[2n+1]{-A} = -x' the print shows a radical with index 2n+1 over '−A'; this is transcribed correctly.
